pathwayLabel: Out-of-State Licensee Examination Route — No Reciprocity; Ohio Exam Still Required
examName: OCILB Plumbing contractor examination (PSI, computer-based) — required; Ohio has no Plumbing reciprocity agreement with Florida
steps: Ohio has no Plumbing reciprocity agreement with Florida. OCILB's published Plumbing agreements are with Arkansas, Mississippi, and West Virginia; no Florida agreement file exists. Under ORC 4740.08, licensing without examination requires such a written agreement.

Ohio's state Plumbing license is a contractor license for commercial work, issued by the Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board (OCILB) and tied to a 'contracting company' — the same license level as Florida's Certified Plumbing Contractor contractor license.

Instead of reciprocity, OCILB's Out-of-State Examination Application offers a route for holders of an out-of-state trades contractor license 'substantially similar' to the Ohio license (ORC Chapter 4796). It replaces Ohio's usual five-years-as-a-tradesperson requirement, but the Ohio examination is still required.
needs_review: whether a Florida Plumbing license is 'substantially similar' to Ohio's Plumbing contractor license is OCILB's case-by-case judgment — Ohio law does not define the standard.

Document: the Florida license held for at least 5 years (e.g., a letter of good standing); at least five building permits issued under that license; at least one tax return showing income earned under it (plus one W-2 if not an owner); and that your contracting company is registered in Ohio as a foreign corporation or foreign LLC with a designated in-state agent.
Maintain contractor's liability insurance of at least $500,000 in a single contracting company's name.

Pay the $25 application fee. Once approved (approval is valid for one year), complete BCI and FBI background checks, then schedule the PSI computer-based exam; PSI's exam fee is not published in the application.
After passing both sections, send the exam results, a $25 license fee, and a certificate of liability insurance; the license and insurance must be assigned to a contracting company.
notes: Ohio side confirmed 2026-09-30 by direct pdftotext extraction of OCILB's Out-of-State Examination Application (form dated 9/2025; server Last-Modified 2026-02-03), downloaded from dam.assets.ohio.gov. Item 8 covers 'an individual who holds an out-of-state trades contractors license, as defined in section 4796.01 ORC, that is substantially similar to the license for which the individual is applying'; the form states OCILB 'issues state licenses to Electrical, HVAC, Refrigeration, Plumbing, and Hydronics Contractors who perform commercial work'; fees are $25 application and $25 license. Reciprocity: OCILB's per-state agreement PDFs were fetched and extracted — Plumbing appears in the Arkansas, Mississippi, and West Virginia agreements; a Florida agreement file returns 404. Florida side: CILB certifies individuals ('Florida issues licenses to individuals based on their qualifications', CILB 10), and current CILB 32 (Ref-17723) lists only Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina for General/Building/Residential. PROVENANCE: the ORC texts are official text from codes.ohio.gov, retrieved and extracted by a helper tool (WebFetch) on the user's side, not read directly by Claude Code; codes.ohio.gov refused connections from this environment and every com.ohio.gov page returned 404 here. ORC 4740.08 (summarized, not verbatim): licensing without examination requires a written reciprocity agreement and 'substantially equal' requirements. ORC 4796.01 (verbatim excerpt as provided): 'out-of-state occupational license' means 'a license, certificate, registration, permit, card, or other authority that is issued or conferred by one of the uniformed services or the government of another state to an individual by which the individual has or claims the privilege to engage in a profession, occupation, or occupational activity'; no general definition of 'substantially similar' appears. Note that OCILB's form refers to an 'out-of-state trades contractors license, as defined in section 4796.01 ORC', a term that excerpt does not itself define. Visual verification is recommended when access allows. Ohio's state license covers commercial work; how residential plumbing work is regulated in Ohio was not confirmed from an official source here. feeUsd is the $25 application fee only; the $25 license fee and PSI's exam fee are separate.
officialSourceName: Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board (OCILB), Ohio Department of Commerce
